rule: A dataclass field whose default is a collection literal is initialized freshly per instance, never emitted as a C# default-parameter value; function-parameter collection defaults stay refused (SPY0400).
principle: A default that C# cannot hold as a constant is evaluated per instance where a constructor body exists, refused where only a parameter default exists.
tension: R-R: Function/lambda parameter non-constant defaults are refused (SPY0401) while dataclass field defaults are lowered; two treatments for similar defaults.
note: Python rejects a mutable dataclass default (ValueError) unless default_factory; Sharpy admits it with default_factory semantics. Also schedules landing with #1685.

rule: A conditional expression whose branches have incompatible types takes their nearest common ancestor type, falling back to object.
principle: The compiler may infer an unwritten common ancestor type for differing branches.
tension: R-W: Superseded: R-W forbids the compiler inventing an ancestor and refuses instead.

rule: isinstance checks against a constructed generic type such as list[int] are supported with full reified narrowing, not parked.
principle: Where the CLR keeps generic type arguments at run time, Sharpy exposes reified checks Python cannot do.
note: Mostly a scheduling decision (unpark, ship in a batch); classified by the user-visible admission. Python raises TypeError for parameterized generics in isinstance.

rule: A bare sequence pattern against an open (non-closed) scrutinee is refused with a steer to a typed class pattern like case list[int]([1, 2]); closed scrutinees still match.
principle: Type tests on erased generic shapes must name the full type argument; never match on an erased shape.
tension: A2: Python matches a bare sequence pattern against any sequence.
note: Extends an unnumbered earlier 'erasure-retired' ruling, so law is empty; related to R-C's reified isinstance.

rule: A coercion that is statically impossible is refused at semantic time with a steer, uniformly for as? and as!, and never lowered to a constant None.
note: T2 picks compile error over runtime/constant result; C# also rejects impossible 'as' conversions (CS0039).

rule: The safe cast as? yields the strict Optional[T]; strict T? versus loose T | None remains a type-level distinction, and as? T? stays refused (SPY0334).
principle: Safe operations that may produce absence return the strict Optional, not a loose nullable.
note: Status quo kept; the reported disagreement was a display bug.

rule: Optional construction is fully strict: no implicit T to T? conversion, bare None is not a T? value, Some(v)/None() are the only constructors, and maybe is the sole bridge from T | None.
principle: An Optional converts implicitly in no direction; every wrap and unwrap is spelled.
tension: R-T: R-T re-wraps a payload store into a narrowed T? implicitly, an implicit T-to-T? conversion in one position.; A2: Python spells absence with bare None everywhere; callers of T? = None() parameters must write Some(v).
note: CV today states bare None is null and None() is the Optional variant; AP one-way/no-magic covers sole constructors. Law may postdate the ruling.

rule: A type whose supertype closure contains the same generic interface at two different instantiations is refused when a Sharpy declaration introduces the second, naming both paths; duplicates entirely inside a CLR type are exempt.
principle: Refuse a construct that would make Sharpy's own dispatch ambiguous, even if C# permits it; park the relaxation.
tension: A1: C# permits implementing one generic interface at two non-unifying instantiations; the refusal is stricter than .NET.

rule: Union, delegate and type-alias declarations nested inside a class body are supported.
note: C# allows nested types; one rule for every host. No rejected options listed.

rule: A list-shaped assignment target like [a, b] = xs is accepted by normalizing it to the tuple-target form in the parser; an augmented assignment to a list target stays refused.
note: Python accepts both spellings and rejects the augmented form; no .NET conflict.

rule: The common type of a conditional's branches is recorded as a node-keyed semantic fact merged by MergeFrom; value positions cast one branch to it and truthiness tests distribute per branch; the emitter never casts on its own.
tension: R-W: R-W later replaces how the join type is computed (best-common-type instead of ancestor join).
note: Row cites 'Rule 2'.

rule: Synthesized protocol interfaces count as ancestors of a type, with their synthesis hoisted into declaration resolution; the join use is superseded and the hoist survives only for the duplicate-instantiation closure check.
principle: Compiler-synthesized interfaces are part of a type's supertype closure for conformance checks.
tension: R-W: Join half superseded by best-common-type.; R-H: The surviving hoist exists to feed R-H's closure check.

rule: Code after a with whose manager may suppress exceptions is reachable, so a non-None function that can fall off there is refused (SPY0266) with a steer; -> None functions are clean.
note: Also excludes a 4-parameter __exit__ refinement and co-lands three issues.

rule: A yield inside a with whose manager can suppress exceptions is refused by name; a ? early-return there is accepted under R-M's reachability rule.
principle: A C# hard constraint (no yield inside try with catch) surfaces as a named Sharpy refusal.
tension: A2: Python permits yield inside any with block.
note: Second half is precedent R-M. Basis inferred from C#'s CS1626; the row gives no reason.

rule: Strict-Optional enforcement lands in the first batch of its group at the seam that batch builds, the group splits into two plans, and the guard is a Roslyn semantic-model scan of snapshots for implicit Optional conversions.
note: Guard choice is a test-instrument element.

rule: Literal-derived strings (PEP 675) are tracked as one node-keyed fact while the expression type stays str, consumed by the store seam in every position, with forms extended later.
principle: A refinement of a type is a recorded fact on the expression, not a new expression type.
note: Python's LiteralString is checker-only; Sharpy follows PEP 675 forms.

rule: A reopened issue is placed in a named batch with acceptance defined as its allowlist rows draining; re-citing the rows to a fresh issue number is rejected.
note: Gap-discovery allowlist rows are deleted on fix, not re-pointed.

rule: One predicate decides which parameter defaults C# can emit as constants across all three hosts; Some(...) and tuple defaults are refused (SPY0401) steering to = None() plus x ??= Some(v); lambdas share def's emission.
principle: A parameter default C# cannot hold as a constant is refused with a steer, never lowered through a sentinel; forward overloads may come later.
tension: R-A: Dataclass collection defaults are lowered per instance while parameter defaults are refused.
note: Rejected nullable sentinel (B); forward-overload synthesis (C) recorded as future. One predicate for three hosts follows T4.

rule: Bare Some, None(), Ok and Err are the only spellings of the Optional and Result constructors; qualified forms are refused by name and the names reserved, while user unions keep Union.Case(...).
note: AP: one way to do the same thing.

rule: Inside a narrowing, a store to the narrowed T? name accepts the payload type and is re-wrapped, the narrowing survives, and a narrowed read into a slot of the declared T? type passes the Optional through.
principle: A narrowed Optional behaves as its payload for stores and reads, with wrapping inserted at the declared slot.
tension: R-G: Re-wrapping a payload store is an implicit T-to-T? conversion that R-G otherwise retires.
note: Tuple-element arm deferred.

rule: in/not in follow the promotion rule (a constant needle converts, a variable needle is refused by name), and CLR constructor calls are checked against bridged parameter types, refusing only on definite mismatch.
principle: The checker refuses only a definite mismatch; where the bridge cannot map a CLR type, it stays silent rather than guess.
note: Bundles two routes under one call-route seam.

rule: A walrus expression's type is what its target reads as immediately after the store, after seam conversion and rebinding narrowing.
principle: An assignment expression evaluates to what the target holds afterwards, not to the raw right-hand side.

rule: Several expressions' common type follows C#'s best-common-type: the slot directs it when one exists; otherwise one operand's type must accept all others; otherwise refuse with an annotate steer. Tuples iterate; count/index are refused.
principle: The compiler never invents a type: the common type is stated by the slot or is one of the operands' own types.
tension: R-B: Supersedes R-B's nearest-common-ancestor rule.; R-L: Supersedes R-L's join half.; A2: Python allows heterogeneous displays without annotation.
note: Cites C# spec section, not an axiom ID. Bundles tuple-iteration decisions, which are choices.

rule: d[k] ??= v requires the key to exist and raises KeyError when it is missing (setdefault handles absence); ??= is statement-only; whether the store is skipped when present is left to the plan.
note: C# Dictionary indexer getter throws on a missing key, so ??= on it raises; option A (hand-rolled lowering) recorded as future.

rule: In a method, a bare store to a name declared in the enclosing class or struct body is refused by name with two steers; a bare read is unresolved (SPY0200) with a self. steer.
principle: A store Python would silently make a new local, when it likely meant a member, is refused with a steer.
tension: N6: N6 says a bare store assigns a binding of the same function, i.e. a fresh local as in Python.; A2: Python accepts the store as a new local.
note: Replaces an ICE. Relaxation to Python's fresh local is parked (#1804).

rule: Dereferencing a loose T | None value without narrowing is accepted by design, per the spec's loose family; an opt-in warning for unnarrowed dereference is parked.
note: Spec file inferred; row says 'per spec + #882'. Also files a sibling issue on index/slice.

rule: A bare None has no type in best-common-type, so a slot-less literal or conditional containing one is refused with the annotate steer; None alone stays SPY0227.
note: Widening to T | None parked as additive future.

rule: A const declared in an interface is legal and emitted as a C# const; the spec is expanded accordingly, never a refusal or property.
note: Row reasons from C# 8 permitting it; spec expanded to match.

rule: A class named like its file stays merged into the module class (other kinds refused); qualification bugs are fixed through universal global:: qualification instead.
principle: A closed one-way design visible to C# consumers is not reopened to fix an implementation bug; fix the helper.
note: Keeps a prior design; door refers to the naming design.

rule: In a method, a bare store to any name resolving to a member of the enclosing class or struct, own or inherited, field or property, is refused (SPY0606) with the same steers.
tension: N6: N6 makes a bare store a fresh local of the function.; A2: Python accepts these stores as locals.
note: Also T4/T1: one membership rule, no silent local.

rule: A walrus binding of None directly under a store slot takes the slot's type, as g(None) does; in any other position it is refused like x = None (SPY0227), and a void-call walrus is refused everywhere.
note: Slot-directed typing extends R-W arm 1 and R-AB; strict slots still refuse through the seam.

rule: Overload resolution follows C#'s ordering: keyword arguments count for applicability and betterness, inference failure makes a candidate inapplicable, and constructor ambiguity is refused (SPY0353) rather than left to Roslyn.
note: Cites C# spec section. Also schedules a new group.

rule: list, set and dict are invariant in their type arguments; read-only interfaces keep their declared out T, and a widened write slot is refused at the slot with a read-only steer.
note: Row: same syntax and restriction as C#.

rule: A local assigned inside a suppression-capable with body and read after is checked at run time with an assigned flag, raising UnboundLocalError on an unset read.
principle: When a flow-sensitive refusal would reject valid Python programs, Sharpy matches Python's run-time error instead.
tension: T2: Picks a run-time error over the previously applied compile-time default.
note: Row does not acknowledge T2; rationale is Python parity (python3 verified).

rule: Numeric literal widening in a slot-less display (int widened to float) is a documented deviation from Python, with a permanent differential-test row.
A parenthesized callee such as (f)(x) is treated exactly as the callee.
note: Also drains allowlist rows.

rule: and/or keep returning bool as the spec states; the issue becomes a steer from the type error toward ??; do not re-propose.
tension: A2: Python's and/or return an operand value.
note: Door refers to changing it later.

rule: tuple[T, ...] (and ... in type arguments such as Callable[..., T]) is refused by name in the parser with a list[T]/Sequence[T] steer; support is parked.
principle: An unsupported Python form is refused by name now, keeping later support additive.
note: Row says refuse-to-support is additive but names no door type.

rule: The registry's protocol table can only add protocol memberships; absent a positive registry answer, membership falls through to the CLR checks.
principle: A registry overlay may add capabilities but never subtract what the CLR shape shows; one authority per answer.
note: Could be read as implementation; classified language because protocol membership widens accepted programs.

rule: Sharpy's Dict supports None keys through an internal null-key slot beside the wrapped .NET Dictionary, with the user surface unchanged.
principle: Restricting an already admitted type is a one-way door; prefer run-time support.
note: Thin-wrapper bridge reconciles .NET's null-key ban with Python; compile-time refusal rejected.

rule: PascalCase CLR member spellings on a Sharpy builtin receiver are refused by name (SPY0203) with the Sharpy spelling as steer; the backtick escape remains.
note: Rejected option was a dual API.

rule: Every non-Sharpy CLR type symbol, generic or not, is emitted through the single qualification authority; no per-namespace using list.
note: Mostly implementation; user sees fixed name collisions.

rule: @property and its setter/getter/deleter decorators are a named parser refusal steering to property get p(self) -> T:, and an executing spec-block sweep is built now.
tension: A2: Python's @property is the idiomatic spelling.
note: Bundles doc fixes and a test-instrument (spec-block sweep).

rule: The dotnet serialization lock publishes log, cwd and start time, waiters say to report rather than kill, and no heartbeat is added until a quiet holder is measured; guarded by a stub-holder test.
principle: Add a mechanism only after its need is measured.
note: Agent tooling rather than a Sharpy harness.

rule: The lossy-CLR-mapping decline is deleted and SPY0354's CLR candidate-list arm retired, so every CLR overload refusal is explained.
principle: Every refusal explains itself; no silent decline path.
note: Acceptance effect unclear from the row.

rule: A fixed-arity tuple is not truth-testable and stays refused with the reason named in the message; tuple | None keeps its null test, and no always-true lowering is added.
tension: A2: Python tests tuples for truthiness.
note: Row cites the spec's own rule and python3.

rule: A mutable-collection default on a non-nullable dataclass or struct field lowers to a nullable constructor parameter assigned with ?? before PostInit; nullable fields and tuple/Some/call defaults keep their existing refusals.
principle: A default C# cannot express lowers to a nullable C# parameter plus a body null-coalesce, not to synthesized overloads.
note: Python dataclasses reject list defaults outright. Door split: .NET signature one-way, Sharpy side two-way. Adds a sibling refusal (frozen + __post_init__ assignment, CS8852).

rule: Generator expressions are added: parenthesized anywhere, bare only as a sole call argument (else a named parse refusal), typed Iterator[T], lowered to a lazy LINQ chain; async clauses stay refused.
principle: A widely used Python expression form with a clean typed, zero-cost lowering is added rather than refused, and the spec is rewritten to match.
tension: CR7: The spec said the construct did not exist; the ruling rewrites the spec instead of conforming to it.; AP: Adding a construct largely because Python has it is the listed anti-pattern.
note: Rejected option kept the spec with a named refusal.

rule: A member whose PascalCase-mangled name equals its enclosing type's name is refused with a new named code, steering to rename or backtick-escape.
principle: A collision created by name mangling is refused by name with an escape steer, never silently renamed on the public C# surface.
note: Row argues by door asymmetry (refuse->fallback non-breaking, reverse breaking) rather than by a law. Python allows such members.

rule: In project mode a directory named the same as a module file in it is refused with a rename steer now; later, package directories emit as C# namespaces.
principle: Adding a file must never rename the emitted names of unrelated siblings; a layout collision is refused until a structural emission exists.
note: Two phases ruled (a now, c next); option field holds the immediate phase.

rule: as? lowers per conversion-verdict kind with a runtime test: enum to backing always Some, backing to enum Some only if defined, explicit-conversion throw becomes None; a totality guard covers every kind.
note: T1 rules out unconditional Some (silently wrong for undefined enum values); rejecting the refuse-total-kinds option is not decided by a law.

rule: Every refusal site returns a dedicated error type that every check accepts without reporting, distinct from the permissive Unknown type, so one mistake does not cascade into further diagnostics.
principle: One mistake yields one diagnostic: refused expressions carry a poison type later checks accept silently, without suppressing distinct errors.
note: Partly implementation. CR11 disposes of the per-pair-reordering option (cell fix); the first-error-per-span option was rejected on merit.

rule: A user module on the search path resolves before a same-named CLR namespace; the namespace stays reachable via backtick spelling, and a default-on warning at the definition names the shadow and the escape.
principle: Local user code shadows external names with a warning naming the escape; a refusal must not depend on an open-ended external set.
note: Rejected refusal because adding a NuGet reference would newly break existing modules (close to T3, not cited).

rule: A non-producer __iter__/__reversed__ declaration is refused by the dunder signature validator under its existing code; a body returning a non-producer under a producer annotation is SPY0260 at the return slot.
principle: A diagnostic is reported at the seam where the mismatch exists, worded against the user-visible type, one code per contract.

rule: Stdlib documentation renders a module-defined type by its bare name on its own module's page and module-qualified on other pages.
principle: Documentation qualifies a name with its module only when referenced from outside that module.
note: Docs rendering; no law applies.

rule: The spec-block sweep drains in order: a per-file prelude first, then fragment markers for genuine partial residue, then one tracking issue per remaining first-error bucket; the gate glob widens now.
principle: Drain a residue first by the step that lets the most entries pass; mark entries permanently exempt only after that.

rule: str.format keyword fields stay refused with SPY0234, now with a steer to use an f-string or format_map.
note: The rejected option was a rung-4 name-keyed lowering (layer ladder, last resort) and magic; also follows SRP-0002. law_cited rests on the row naming 'rung-4', the CV ladder.

rule: A bound method or CLR method group used as a value is a typed delegate and is not refused; a spec sentence with an executed example documents it.
principle: Refuse only where a type hazard exists; a fully typed common idiom is not refused by position.
note: Ruled 'as designed'; no behaviour change.

rule: Spec-block residue gets a dedicated last work group plus a standing rule to drain entries whenever a change touches them.
principle: A residue gets a scheduled drain group plus drain-on-touch; a tracker alone never drains and blind mass-marking hides bugs.

rule: CLR interface sequence and mapping types keep CLR identity; list(x), dict(x) or set(x) is the only conversion, and implicit slot materialization is replaced by a type mismatch with a steer.
principle: A CLR-typed value keeps its CLR identity; conversion to a Sharpy collection is always explicit, never implicit at a slot.
note: AP 'no magic' (owner quote) rules out the implicit options; T1 rules out copy-everywhere (silently lost mutation); AP wrapper types rules out the view adapter.

rule: The let-declaration work runs last after P20 in three sub-phases (stage 1, codemod and migration, stage 2), each its own plan and measured gate.
tension: R-CN: R-CN reverses this sequencing once its premise was gone.

rule: let lands as an unconditional keyword with no experimental feature flag, because the design is ruled and the large migration cannot run behind a gate.
principle: A ruled design lands ungated; feature flags are for designs still under evaluation.
note: Departs from the default-off experimental-feature convention (CLAUDE.md, not in the law table); the row gives its reason.

rule: := keeps declare-if-new, rebind-if-existing semantics and remains the only expression-position introducer after let's stage 2.
note: python3 runs the same program with the same meaning (A2 twin); current behaviour already correct (T3).

rule: Assignment to an undeclared name gets one new code steering to let; module-scope non-const bindings reuse SPY0340 with the steer that module-scope bindings are const.
principle: A new code only where the cure differs; reuse an existing code when its steer fits.
tension: N1: N1 lists let, var and module variables as module-level declarations, while this row refuses non-const module-scope bindings.
note: Code choice is diagnostic; the module-scope const restriction it states is a language fact ruled elsewhere.

rule: out let x introduces a new binding and out x writes through to an existing one, mirroring C# out var x and out x.
principle: Every introduction site is spelled with let; no position declares-if-new except walrus.
note: Precedent is the let binding law (assignment never declares) of the same design; mirrors C# where Python has no twin.

rule: str/repr of defaultdict render the factory as a fixed placeholder, defaultdict(<factory>, {...}), documented as a deviation.
principle: When Python's output needs source information the runtime lacks, print a fixed documented placeholder, never CLR text or compiler-injected names.
tension: R-CJ: R-CJ makes str/repr of every Stdlib type COMPARED, while this row keeps a documented deviation for defaultdict.
note: CV ladder rules out the name-keyed option; leaking the CLR delegate spelling was rejected on merit. FS lists this as ruled.

rule: Non-generic CLR interfaces keep CLR identity with no object fallback; unmapped types are refusal-only for pointers/by-ref, interface satisfaction is proven by reflection, and the checker picks Roslyn's overload.
note: CR11 also rejects the per-formal cell fix.

rule: A bare tuple annotation is refused with a steer to () or tuple[()] for the empty tuple or tuple[T, ...]; any-arity tuples stay parked.
note: Python's meaning (any arity) has no CLR representation, so A1 wins; giving it the empty meaning was rejected as surprising (A2 evidence).

rule: A parenthesized (A, B) in expression-position type arguments is one tuple[A, B] argument, matching the annotation shorthand, not Python's flattening to two arguments.
note: 'Rule 7' read as CR7 (the spec is authoritative).

rule: Named parameters in function type annotations stay refused (SPY0104) and the spec section describing them is deleted.
tension: CR7: The ruling changes the spec to match the implementation, the reverse of CR7.
note: Owner acknowledges deleting the spec; reason is A1 (no CLR delegate carries parameter names).

rule: repr of PEP 750 Interpolation and Template uses CPython 3.14's constructor spelling, reachable through user-facing repr().
note: FS row cites this very ruling (codified after the fact).

rule: A BCL collection exposing Count has __len__ for len, bool and truth testing via one shared reflective predicate.
note: Rejected refusal would turn running programs into refusals (T3).

rule: Calling an instance method via a CLR-backed builtin type name (str.upper(...)) is refused with SPY0290, as for user classes; a same-named CLR static is steered to the backtick escape.
principle: Builtin types follow the same member-access rules as user classes; no Python behaviour is added for builtins alone.
tension: A2: Python runs str.upper('a') with the same meaning, so A2 offers a twin that the ruling declines without naming an A1 conflict.
note: Python unbound-method semantics rejected as one-way and builtin-only.

rule: Using a call that returns no value as a value is a new compile error in every value position and for every callee kind; statement position stays valid.
note: Row: 'Type Safety over Python syntax'; Python would yield None.

rule: A bad spec passed through a format method-group delegate is a runtime ValueError only; no compile-time check follows the delegate.
principle: Static checks bind to symbols; a value invoked as a delegate gets only the runtime check until symbol facts flow through conversions.
tension: T2: A compile error was available (carry the origin symbol's facts) but deferred.
note: Row does not acknowledge T2; it calls the class cure two-way and able to land later.

rule: Core exposes one pure format-spec validator used by both the runtime formatter and the compiler's static check, retiring the duplicated mirror.
principle: One behaviour has one implementation; a compile-time check calls the runtime's pure function instead of mirroring it.
note: Later cited as 'the R-BX shape' by R-CG.

rule: A non-empty format spec on an operand type without __format__ (list, dict, set, tuple, plain user class) is a runtime TypeError, and SPY0609 when the spec is a literal, on every route.
note: Programs that previously ran padded now refuse (verified by direction).

rule: Emitting user types beside the module class is its own plan right after the package-namespace plan, which first settles the module-as-namespace layout.
note: Folding in was rejected because the earlier plan's byte-identical acceptance would become uncheckable (layout changes land alone). Door is about module-function FQNs moving.

rule: An interface member named _m or __m is refused with a new code steering to drop the underscore; a backtick-escaped spelling emits verbatim as a public member.
note: Interface members are public in .NET; emitting public silently would claim a protection the runtime lacks.

rule: A user def __format__ synthesizes an IFormattable implementation whose ToString(format, provider) calls __format__.
note: Dunder-to-CLR-interface synthesis is the zero-cost bridge; rejected option was a name-keyed suppression (CV rung 4).

rule: Formatting with an empty spec follows Python: IFormattable values use ToString("", invariant), everything else uses str; a plain f-string hole calls Format only for Formattable/Unknown kinds.
note: Output moves only for types that opted into IFormattable.

rule: The static format-spec walk stops at a nested-spec field and at a non-empty spec on an Unknown-kind operand, leaving those to the runtime ValueError.
principle: Static checking stops where operand kind or spec is not statically known; the runtime check answers there.
tension: T2: A compile error is given up for a runtime error where a partial static decision was possible.

rule: A literal format template with an out-of-range index or unmatched keyword field is a new compile error, and the runtime keyword error text becomes Python's KeyError: 'name'.
note: T2 rules out runtime-only; new code vs reusing SPY0609 is a choice (one contract, one explanation).

rule: One Python-name authority spells runtime type names: Python names for Core/Stdlib/CLR kinds, source names for user types; enum str prints Color.RED and repr <Color.RED: 1>.
principle: Runtime-visible names use one Python-spelling authority; a user type prints its source name, never its CLR name.
note: FS rows cite this ruling (codified after it).

rule: The member-name mangling rule moves into Core and the compiler delegates to it; runtime attribute lookup tries the mangled name then verbatim.
str of an Optional is transparent (1 or None), while repr uses the constructor spelling Some(1) or None() on both variants.
note: No Python twin; Nullable<T>.ToString precedent (A1); str output on four routes is kept (T3). repr(None()) changes.

rule: Exception message text beyond the type name is a deviation by default, recorded as a ledger row; a message quoted in the spec stays compared.
tension: R-CE: R-CE makes runtime KeyError text match Python although message text is deviation by default.
note: FS row codifies this very ruling; judged against today's text per brief.

rule: str/repr of every Stdlib type is compared with Python, one tracker per type family, each type implementing IRepr with a constructor-spelled repr.
principle: A fidelity channel is promoted whole for a type family, never per type.
tension: R-BN: R-BN keeps defaultdict's repr as a documented deviation.
note: FS row codifies this ruling.

rule: Which operand a sort refusal names stays a deviation (inherited .NET algorithm), but key= is called exactly once per element, as in Python.
principle: Algorithm-internal order inherited from .NET may differ; a side-effect count a user can observe must match Python.
note: Split ruling: one half deviation, one half compared.

rule: Every Core and Stdlib text path uses the invariant culture, matching CPython's C locale; current-culture output is a bug.
principle: Program output never depends on the host's locale or culture.
note: FS row codifies this ruling.

rule: A surface not listed in the Python-fidelity table is a deviation until an owner ruling promotes it; the next long-tail cell is a ledger row, not an issue.
principle: Python-fidelity obligations open only by explicit ruling, never by an auditor's python3 diff.
note: FS's default clause is this ruling's text.

rule: The remaining let-declaration sub-phases run next, before P15, with silent-wrong binding fixes ahead of the codemod; this replaces R-BI's sequencing only.
principle: When a ruling's stated premise is gone, its sequencing is revisited; silent-wrong fixes precede work built on the same facts.
tension: R-BI: Supersedes R-BI's order (P21 after P20).
note: Cites R-BI explicitly as the ruling it revises.

rule: All Python string-literal prefixes (rf, fr, rb, br, tr, rt) are accepted in any order and case; doubled braces, backslash escapes and line continuations in format specs work; one lexer table drives the editor grammar.
principle: A Python lexical surface is taken whole from one table rather than admitted piecemeal with per-case refusals.
note: A2 favours it but does not decide; rejected options were rejected on complexity grounds. Row says 'Additive'.

rule: A user __repr__ implements the repr channel separately from __str__ (which stays ToString); a class defining only __str__ reprs as <mod.C object>, as in Python.
note: FS lists repr of user classes as COMPARED; row cites precedent R-CF.

rule: .name and .value work on CLR interop enums as on Sharpy enums: .name gives the member name, .value the underlying integer.
note: Cites the '#2007 all System.Enum' ruling; #2007 is in R-CF's class. Row says 'Additive'.

rule: Every function, including main, emits its ordinary mangled name (main becomes Main) in every module kind; the executable entry point is chosen by a compilation option instead of a MainFunc rename.
principle: A name follows one mangling rule everywhere; special cases are moved to compiler options, never to per-name renames.
tension: T4: Supports it by analogy (one rule over a special case), though T4 names hosts, not names.
note: Option is an owner-coined c-prime. Reason given: two spelling rules for one name.

rule: Class, struct, enum, union and interface declarations and imports inside a function are refused with one new validation code steering to module or class level.
principle: A Python construct the CLR lacks, whose emulation would change other semantics for no type-system payoff, is refused with a steer rather than emulated.
note: Today it silently compiles unbound (T1 argues for some fix, not for refuse over support). A1 noted (C# has no local types) but hoisting was possible.

rule: A Stdlib module's type is reachable only through its module; a bare type name not imported is SPY0202 with an import steer, except an explicit spec-cited Core interop roster.
note: Python raises NameError on the same program (twin exists). Row says 'Relaxable'.

rule: Mutable containers and tuples or records containing them are unhashable: a compile-time refusal at hash(), dict-key and set-element positions plus a runtime TypeError twin.
note: Row cites 'spec promises a refusal' and 'Type Safety over Python syntax' (axiom precedence).

rule: A local module binds before stdlib, referenced libraries and CLR namespaces, as Python's sys.path order; only referenced assemblies count; a default-on warning names the shadow.
principle: What a process happened to load at run time never decides a binding; only declared references do.
note: Rejected refusal would refuse Python-legal layouts; A2 twin decides. The loaded-assembly principle is new.

rule: Underscore-prefixed module variables are module-private like underscore module functions: importing or qualifying them from another module is SPY0283, decided by one access authority.
principle: A naming convention carries the same meaning for every kind of declaration it applies to.
tension: A2: Python lets `from lib import _w` run; Sharpy refuses a program with a twin.
note: Row says 'Refusal, relaxable'. Builds on the existing private-function rule (not cited by R-id).

rule: `from pkg import sub` binds a child submodule when __init__ does not export the name; a directory without __init__.spy stays refused with a steer to add one.
principle: A Python import form is admitted where it has a definite anchor file; layouts making every directory importable are refused with a steer.
note: Python matches for submodule binding, deviates for namespace packages. Row: (a) to (b) later is additive.

rule: Redeclaring an annotated module-level name is refused with SPY0204, as a repeated const already is, instead of silently keeping the first value.
note: Today prints the first value silently; Python rebinds (rejected because module scope is const-only after P21c).

rule: A member's declaration fixes its emitted name and every reference uses it, for class members as for enum members; a member declared with backticks is reachable by its plain spelling.
note: Precedent is a plan ruling, not an R-id. Re-pins the #478 test.

rule: lru_cache honours maxsize (None means unbounded, values above the CLR int range saturate with a deviation row), and `from functools import lru_cache` binds the builtin decorator.
principle: A Python stdlib import path naming an existing builtin binds to it; out-of-CLR-range arguments saturate with a recorded deviation rather than refuse.
note: Row says 'Additive'.

rule: strftime %Z uses the C library time-zone name on Unix; on Windows it uses the .NET display name with a deviation row.
tension: T4: Gives a per-OS split, though T4 speaks of program hosts, not operating systems.
note: FS lists strftime/platform text as COMPARED; row cites R-CL. Windows half deviates.

rule: .real and .imag on int and float are not added; their absence is a recorded deviation row, while complex keeps both.
note: FS: unlisted surface is DEVIATION until promoted (R-CM, cited). Row says 'Relaxable'.

rule: All Stdlib modules, spy-sourced and hand-written, move under a stdlib package with __init__.spy, namespaced Sharpy.Stdlib.<Module>, with one prefix-strip rule replacing the python-name map.
principle: The standard library is laid out as ordinary modules under one rule, with no magic stems or name maps.
note: Mostly a layout/implementation change, but renames the public Stdlib C# surface once. AP (no magic, one way) aligns but does not strictly decide among options.

rule: Members whose mangled name differs carry a [SharpyName] attribute, read by one naming policy shared by json, yaml and toml, so field names round-trip losslessly.
principle: Record a source name rather than infer it with a lossy inverse transform.

rule: __name__ on both class and function references compiles: classes via the Python type-name helper, functions via the [SharpyName] attribute on the method; nothing is refused.
note: Row text is the version revised by R-DG; uses layer-ladder rung 3 (CV).

rule: Methods whose emitted name differs from the source get a [SharpyName] attribute, so function objects print <function name>, lambdas <function <lambda>>; nameless closures get one deviation row.
principle: Snapshot churn is no reason to reject a warranted change; keep information once a cheap mechanism exists.
note: Promotes an unlisted FS surface by ruling; addresses omitted as NOT COMPARED.

rule: Two source files mapping to the same dotted module name (derived from the source root by one authority) are refused with a new validation code naming both files.
principle: Module identity comes from one authority; a collision is refused naming both parties, never silently renamed.
note: Rejected rename partly because it is one-way; preference for two-way doors.

rule: Public Core and Stdlib signatures may not use raw .NET container types (KeyValuePair becomes tuple); a commented list exempts IEnumerable and a few interfaces until a Sharpy Iterable spelling exists.
tension: AP: The IEnumerable exemption keeps a raw .NET interface in public APIs for now.
note: Phasing is the owner's choice; the rule itself is the written anti-pattern. One-way per signature for C# consumers.

rule: cache_info() and cache_clear() are members of any function memoized by the cache decorator, recognised from one materialized fact; CacheInfo's str is compared with Python.
principle: A documented surface is implemented rather than withdrawn; prefer the option from which the alternative stays additive.
note: str comparison follows R-CJ.

rule: LSP range formatting returns only the minimal line-diff hunks of the whole-document format that intersect the range, re-checked on the applied text at one formatter seam.
The parser records how the placeholder, empty tuple and empty parentheses were written, and the unparser writes that spelling back unchanged.
principle: Tools preserve the user's written spelling; canonicalization is an opt-in mode, never the default.

rule: Work group P41 runs first after the chores.
CLR reflection skips unloadable types and unresolvable assemblies with a warning naming them and follows type forwards; metadata-only loading is deferred.
note: Warning is user-visible, but row calls both options internal.

rule: C# the emitter synthesizes stays within the netstandard2.1 surface, guarded by compiling the emitted corpus against netstandard2.1 references; no target-framework switch.
note: A1 states generated code targets C# 9.0 for netstandard2.1 compatibility.

rule: Without -n, every module's C# namespace is SharpyApp.<path from the source root>, on every compilation route.
principle: One emitted-namespace rule for every compilation route.

rule: An import cycle compiles only when every symbol imported on every edge is used only in annotations, regardless of entry or file names; otherwise the diagnostic names the offending import use.
principle: A cycle is admitted only when no edge needs a value at load time, judged independently of file names.
tension: CR7: Rewrites the spec's normative 'every cycle is SPY0302' instead of fixing the implementation to it.
note: Compatible with N3 (initialization cycles refused) but N3 does not choose among the options.

rule: `raise` is accepted as the body of a match-expression arm only, lowering to a C# throw expression; it is not a general expression.
principle: Admit the narrowest form of a construct whose general form would be hard to take back.
note: Row says 'Additive'.

rule: Parenthesized `from m import (a, b)` is accepted, and the formatter keeps the written form.
note: Only alternative was parking it.

rule: A match expression written directly inside brackets stays refused, with a steer to bind it to a local first.
principle: A lexer invariant (no significant newlines inside brackets) outranks a syntactic convenience.
note: Row says 'Relaxable later'.

rule: A for loop over range lowers to a C# for loop and nothing more; direct array indexing is not added.
principle: An emission optimisation must not change any value without a proof rule.
tension: T3: Aligns: rejected option would change negative-index behaviour.
note: T3 rules out (b) but not parking.

rule: A dotted CLR type name not bound by an import is refused with the import steer; fully qualified names from referenced assemblies are not a second spelling.
note: AP 'multiple ways to do the same thing'. Consistent with R-CT. Row says 'Relaxable to (b)'.

rule: Members and parameters of nullable-oblivious CLR types accept None when written to and read as non-null T.
tension: R-EH: R-EH supersedes the read half with unknown nullability and a boundary null check.; A3: Reading a possibly-null CLR value as plain T admits null into a non-null slot unchecked.
note: Row acknowledges (b) as the sound option. Read half superseded by R-EH.

rule: Comparing a CLR reference with == None or != None is refused with an `is None` steer; a CLR implicit conversion to bool joins the single truthiness predicate.
tension: R-EH: R-EH says `T | None == None` on a CLR reference stays admitted; boundary of the refusal needs checking.
note: Part 1 rests on 'two spellings' (AP); part 2 is a choice. Part 1 relaxable, part 2 additive.

rule: `type(X)` where X names a type means the CLR typeof(X) in every expression position; Python's `type(int) is type` differs and is recorded as a deviation row.
principle: Reuse an existing Python spelling for the CLR concept rather than add a builtin; record the mismatch as a deviation.
note: Rejecting (c) follows AP; choosing (a) over (b) does not.

rule: CLR enum members and constants resolve by their screaming-caps spelling, the verbatim CLR name keeps working, and an unknown member is SPY0203 with a did-you-mean.
tension: AP: Two accepted spellings for one member is 'multiple ways to do the same thing'.
note: Rejected (a) ignores the spec convention; (c) breaks running programs.

rule: A bare `_` as an assignment target is a discard; only the backticked `_` is an ordinary identifier.
principle: A Python idiom's dominant meaning wins over its literal semantics when keeping both needs a second spelling.
tension: A2: Python binds `_` as a normal variable readable afterwards.
note: Reverses plan-be89c1 D1 (a) for the bare spelling.

rule: Names dispatched by reflection must use the backtick spelling; this is by design, recorded in one spec sentence, with no acronym table or near-miss warning.
principle: The name mangler stays one mechanical rule; exceptions are written with the backtick escape, not encoded in tables.

rule: An issue about SPY0606 is folded into an existing tracker rather than relaxing SPY0606 to a warning now.
principle: Do not relax a refusal that an already-scheduled change would re-tighten.

rule: `type` stays a hard keyword; using it as a name gives a diagnostic naming the keyword and the backtick escape.
principle: A keyword collision is answered by naming the backtick escape in the diagnostic, not by softening the keyword.
note: Soft keyword rejected 'for now'.

rule: In emitted test files, `assert x in c` lowers to Assert.True over the ordinary membership lowering for every container, and the files disable the related xUnit analyzer warnings.
principle: An operator has one lowering everywhere; host-specific analyzer noise is silenced in the emitted file, not in project config.
note: Could be read as implementation; users' test projects observe it.

rule: The CI matrix is written on a branch and verified by a PR run whose counts are compared with the sequential control before merging.
principle: A change to the gate instrument is proven against the existing control before it replaces it.
note: VC6 concerns the gate but does not decide this.

rule: System.Object members bind on Sharpy class instances, landing with the inherited-member-name group; until then the refusal stands.
note: A1: Sharpy classes are CLR objects; CV layer ladder rejects the name-keyed option. Scheduling half is process.

rule: Unannotated CLR references have unknown nullability: usable as T, testable with `is None`, maybe-wrappable, null-checked when stored into a non-null slot; a None test on declared non-null T is refused.
principle: Nullability-oblivious foreign values are platform types: usable directly, checked at the boundary into a declared non-null slot.
tension: R-DW: Supersedes its read half.; T2: The boundary check is a run-time error where a strict T | None reading would give a compile error.
note: Option labelled c+ (owner-coined). Unplaced; lands alone.

rule: The unittest assert_in and assert_not_in marker calls are type-checked like the expression `x in c` and lowered to an assertion on that ordinary lowering, rather than being retired or kept on a contains-assertion.
principle: A member of a library family is not retired piecemeal; the whole family keeps one consistent treatment.
note: Argument is family consistency; no written law names it. Python twin is assertIn, which also uses `in`.

rule: `is None` and `is not None` are a pure reference null check on every reference type and never run user code; the `==` operator synthesized from `__eq__` is null-safe.
principle: `is` never runs user code; `==` always runs the type's equality. Operator meaning never depends on where the operator was declared.
tension: R-DX: Rewords R-DX part 1's steer and supersedes the dotnet_interop.md sentence that `is None` honours an overloaded `==`.; A1: Changes behaviour of CLR types with overloaded `==` (Unity destroyed objects now compare non-None).
note: Owner framed it as least cognitive load; Python's `is` identity twin and one-rule (T4) decide it, rejected (c) leaves a NullReferenceException (T1/T2).

rule: A `.spyproj` Reference item honours HintPath as the assembly path with Include as the name; without HintPath, Include is the path; an unresolved reference is a diagnostic.
principle: Project files honour the established MSBuild metadata conventions instead of inventing or ignoring them.
note: Arguably A1 (follow .NET conventions), but A1 is about runtime semantics, so classed choice.

rule: Making module search paths reach import resolution is filed as a standalone chore now rather than cured inside the namespaces group or kept in its current group.
note: Ordering only.

rule: LSP code-action shape preservation becomes its own work group scheduled directly after the preceding LSP group, not folded into it.
A new work group runs directly after a named predecessor group and absorbs one of that group's issues as its first phase.
note: Ordering only.

rule: One work group covers the whole unittest assert marker family, generated against the plain-assert twin, instead of fixing only assert_in and assert_not_in.
tension: R-EI: Widens R-EI's two-marker fix to the whole family.
note: Class before cell and generator-first decide (b).

rule: Accepts the proposed ordering of four work groups and puts the `is None` chore first among chores.
In project mode, an import that resolves to a `.spy` file outside the project's declared source set is refused with a diagnostic, rather than silently compiling the import closure.
principle: When a design question is open, refuse now: a refusal can be relaxed later, an acceptance cannot be withdrawn.
note: The reversible-refusal preference recurs (R-FA, R-FH) but is not a written law.

rule: A per-alternative guard in a match arm tests truthiness, the same as the whole-arm guard, instead of requiring bool in either or both positions.
tension: R-EU: R-EU makes the two guard positions differ for narrowing, after this ruling made them alike for truthiness.
note: (b) breaks running arm guards (T3); (c) keeps two rules (T4). Owner asked what C# does (bool-only `when`) and departed from it.

rule: `== None` and `!= None` compile on every .NET reference type and run that type's own `==` operator; the earlier refusal is lifted for CLR types.
tension: R-DX: Lifts R-DX part 1's refusal for CLR types.
note: Row says 'follows from R-EJ'.

rule: The formatter keeps up to one user-written blank line between statements, rather than fully canonical layout or layout preserved exactly as written.
principle: Tools keep a bounded amount of user layout intent rather than either erasing it or preserving it verbatim.

rule: A guard that gates a whole match arm narrows types in the arm body; a per-alternative guard never narrows, even as the sole alternative.
principle: Narrowing follows exactly what gates the whole region, as C# flow analysis does; no special cases.
tension: R-ER: R-ER aligned the two guard positions on truthiness; this ruling splits them on narrowing.
note: Row argues one rule and C#'s flow analysis; (b) rejected for forcing an if-twin, not by a law.

rule: Where a CPython stdlib function uses a sentinel default, the Sharpy source offers an overload without that parameter (applying the real default) and one with it, explicit None meaning the Python value.
principle: A Python sentinel default is modelled by overloads, never by a magic in-band default value.
note: Rejected (a) a deviation on a COMPARED surface (FS); (c) magic default (AP); rung 1 is the layer ladder (CV).

rule: The frozenset `== null` deviation is kept with its stated reason corrected: user programs lower `== None` to a null test; only Core's C# and C# consumers bear the residual cost.
principle: Do not promote a deviation when doing so makes the C# consumer surface ambiguous; keep the reversible option.
note: Door inferred from '(a)->(b) is additive later' stated in the row.

rule: Concurrency defects become their own work group whose first step is a thread-concurrency harness over a compile/load/stdlib by thread-count matrix with an allowlist ratchet, before fixing the seams.
note: A 3x3 matrix requires a generator first (contract section 11).

rule: A set of small issues ship as ordered chores, measurement chores carrying their table in the commit body, rather than one plan with a gate.
principle: A day of work does not get a plan and verify round; it goes as chores.

rule: Accepts a batch of reorderings, moves an earlier group forward so a dependent group does not land short, and folds, posts or closes several issues.
When a stdlib callable accepts a call CPython rejects, a harmless widening (re endpos=None) is a deviation row, while one users would come to depend on (hmac without digestmod) is refused.
principle: An extra acceptance is recorded only if no valid program changes meaning; otherwise refuse, because a refusal can be relaxed but a kept acceptance cannot.
note: Split ruling: hmac part matches Python (refuse); endpos part deviates.

rule: A stdlib default-parameter audit becomes its own group with the widened audit (spy-sourced and hand-written C#, a hand table, each candidate confirmed by a run) first.
note: Row cites contract section 11.

rule: threading.Thread's args and kwargs parameters are not supported; this is a recorded deviation whose steer is to pass a lambda as target.
principle: An untypeable Python variadic API becomes a deviation with a lambda steer, not a family of typed factories or dynamic invocation.
note: (c) is excluded by AP/A3 (runtime type checking), but (b) is left open by the laws.

rule: A Thread's default name is `Thread-N` (the main thread `MainThread`) and name is a non-null str; the Python target suffix is deferred.
note: repr(Thread) COMPARED under R-CJ and FS rules out (c); (b) rejected on schedule.

rule: Thread.ident before start() is a recorded deviation rather than typing ident as `int | None`.
principle: A property is not widened to nullable just to mirror a Python None in a misuse-only state; the gap is recorded.
tension: A3: Python's None-before-start is replaced by a non-null value, close to the kind of default A3 distrusts.
note: Row says the id value is NOT COMPARED, but the None-before-start state is not an id value, so FS does not decide it.

rule: An issue is split at the process-wide-state boundary: stateless cells now, state-adding cells after the concurrency harness group; a related issue is a chore and a group is placed.
principle: Work that adds process-wide state waits for the harness that can measure it; stateless work proceeds now.
note: Rejected (c) cites the shape R-EY rejected (precedent R-EY for that option).

rule: The timeout-conversion tracker is widened to every stdlib seconds parameter across modules, as one stdlib-wide conversion.
note: 'Both fix one arm of a mirrored structure' is VC1 wording.

rule: A timeout above the CLR's int.MaxValue milliseconds but at or below TIMEOUT_MAX saturates at about 24.8 days, recorded as one family deviation row.
principle: A CLR limit below Python's accepted range saturates as a recorded deviation rather than refusing calls Python accepts.
note: Follows existing rows (socket timeout, time.sleep clamp) that are not numbered rulings.

rule: The timeout chore runs first, before an LSP group, since it adds no process-wide state.
note: Applies R-FF's state-boundary principle.

rule: Three design issues are scheduled at proposed positions rather than parked; one remains a parked card.
The literal-loss fact widens: a lex that dropped a line holding a quote, re-paired a triple quote, or stopped at its error budget marks the literal map unknown; a generator comes first.
principle: A repair route refuses only where it detectably lost information, and the detection covers the class, not a list of cells.
note: VC1 (cited as contract section 1) excludes (c) only; (b) rejected on usefulness, so not fully derivable.

rule: Sharpy's subprocess kill, terminate and send_signal deliver the real Unix signal and report negative returncodes like Python; externally signalled children keep 128+N as one deviation row.
note: Python twin exists and the value is COMPARED; (b) misreports a genuine exit 137 (T1).

rule: `-> NoReturn` is the spelling for a non-returning function, lowering to void with DoesNotReturn honoured on every callee; `Never` is refused with a steer; raise-only bodies are not inferred.
principle: Where Python offers several spellings, Sharpy takes one, the one that shadows no user name, and steers the others.
tension: A2: `-> Never` is valid Python (3.11+) yet is refused.
note: One-way-to-do-it (AP) excludes (c) only.

rule: The leading-dot implicit member covers enum members, constants, static fields and properties only, excludes static methods and constructors, and gets a new refusal code with a qualify fix-it.
principle: A context-typed expression takes its type only from a resolved target; anything needing return-type overload resolution waits.
note: Row also says the new diagnostic code is permanent.

rule: A ref to a Sharpy list element is refused with a steer to arrays or spans; ref is allowed for arrays, struct fields, spans, ref/out parameters and locals.
note: (b) brings an aliasing hazard under append that cannot be refused statically; (b) is also a net10-only Core surface, which CR5 permits.

rule: The lex that feeds the indent map continues past its error budget without reporting, so the unread tail gets real tokens and existing repairs are kept.
note: Rejected (c) is 'the direction R-FK rejected'; (b) loses repairs for the same reason R-FK rejected its (b).

rule: A stray triple quote that leaves the lexer signature of a correct document is a permanent documented limit; its rows leave the allowlist and become a census floor.
principle: A case indistinguishable at the available signal is a documented permanent limit measured by a census, not guessed with content heuristics.
note: Sits uneasily with the gap-sweep convention that each allowlist row cites an open issue closed on fix; resolved by a permanent tracker.

rule: The re-pair arm keys on a dropped span holding a quote on the close line, rather than any lexer error there or a growing list of codes.
tension: R-FV: R-FV later narrows this arm to quotes leaving a literal open at line end.
note: Rejected (c) also follows VC1 (the arm recurs at the sixth code).

rule: A stdlib docs generator with a guard twin is a chore in the next slot; an unreachable documented member is filed as a stdlib cell by class at close.
note: Rejecting (b) reuses R-FF's 'adds no process-wide state' reasoning.

rule: An LSP sweep group moves to directly before another so its allowlist drains while the sweep and driver are warm.
A lexer fact records a bracket open at end of file and the recovery line; indent-only routes make no edits below the opener while it is open, keeping repairs above.
principle: Indent repair never acts on a token-level guess whose misses are wrong edits.
note: Rejected (c) is 'the content-heuristic shape R-FQ rejected'.

rule: The re-pair arm narrows: a quote in the given-up span counts only if a literal is still open at the line's end, with each new tail paired with a positive control.
tension: R-FR: Narrows R-FR's chosen arm (b).
note: Rejected (c) widens to the option R-FR rejected; (b) rejected for blindness of the generator, not by law.

rule: A function with a *args tail cannot be used as a function value without a lambda; it is refused in the existing family with a wrap-it-in-a-lambda steer.
note: Rejected (b) is also magic (AP); function types carry no names, defaults or tails per R-BR.

rule: The stale hand-written grammar file is deleted now; an executable grammar derived from the parser is written late in its own group.
principle: An unread hand model is deleted rather than maintained; the replacement is derived from the implementation.
note: Refers to a 2026-07-02 ruling for the predicted measurement.

rule: The spec output-marker mechanism (running blocks, reporting mismatches, seeding prose that states results) is a chore now; converting blocks rides the existing review rule and any plan touching a spec file.
note: Conversions ride R-BG (cited); the timing choice itself is open.

rule: The exact-diagnostic-code oracle fix in the error injector is a chore now; the per-construct census roster and new injections become a group after the concurrency group.
note: Ordering only; test-instrument content.

rule: Four owner-filed sub-issues form one plan in phases under their parent, scheduled after a named group and before two others.
note: Row notes this is an owner structure, not the contract section 10 default.

rule: A mutation-testing pilot runs as a background chore in a lock-idle slot, Lexer first, with a report carrying the command and measured score; survivors become test-gap issues by class.
The round's group order is fixed as proposed, with the stdlib ICE group and the per-module ledger group kept in their proposed late slots rather than pulled forward.
note: Ordering only.

rule: Every indent-only formatting route leaves a comment-only line byte-identical, including its leading whitespace, rather than re-indenting it by column or by the following line.
principle: An editing route that cannot know the structure keeps the user's bytes rather than guessing a repair.

rule: The indent-only formatter residue becomes its own small group directly before the editor block, with its generator extended first and a verify round.
tension: R-GF: The cap ruled next stops this warm-harness slotting from being used again.
note: Generator-first is VC11; the slot itself is the choice. Rejected fold cites R-EM.

rule: The formatter/indent residue family is capped: further residues become cells on an open tracker and queue behind waiting user-facing groups, unless they are regressions against the last pushed sha.
principle: A tooling residue family may not keep jumping the queue; later residues wait behind user-facing silent-wrong work, regressions excepted.
tension: R-GC: R-GC used the warm-harness argument this ruling now caps.; R-GE: R-GE used the same argument once more.
note: Owner-initiated, no option letter.

rule: The one PDB-emitting site emits an explicit portable PDB, guarded by a signature check with a mutation record, as a chore before other work.
principle: A host-breaking release defect is fixed at once as its own chore, not folded into a distant group of a different class.
note: Guard with mutation record is CR12/VC2; the placement and the class judgement are the choice.

rule: Release publishing runs a per-RID smoke of the published artifact, and every push builds and smoke-tests the CLI on a Windows leg; the full Windows test matrix waits for evidence.
note: Additive.

rule: A patch release is cut as soon as the Windows-install fix's gate is green, rather than waiting for the next minor.
principle: A defect that breaks the documented install on a supported host gets an immediate patch release.

rule: The investigation comment with the workaround is posted on the issue immediately, before the placement comment, rather than waiting for the application turn.
principle: Users get a known workaround as soon as it exists, ahead of scheduling.

rule: All three dotnet-launching CLI sites share one preflight that refuses before compiling, naming runtime versus SDK and the install link; an in-process run is parked as a roadmap design.
principle: Check host prerequisites before doing work and refuse with a coded diagnostic, rather than crash after a wasted compile.
note: (b) then (a) stacks; (a) one-way in practice.

rule: A missing dotnet host tool is a new coded diagnostic shared by all launching sites, with an explanation entry; the restore site's uncoded message migrates to it.
principle: Each diagnostic code has one meaning: a new failure axis gets its own code, never a near neighbour's or uncoded stderr text.
note: CR10 forces the explanation entry, not the new-code-vs-reuse choice. Additive.

rule: A per-RID CI job runs the archive with dotnet scrubbed from the path and asserts the new code and exit code, plus a table-driven child-process theory with a path-intact positive control.
principle: An OS-dependent behaviour is checked on every OS it ships for; one platform is not a control for another.
note: Positive control is CR12/VC2; per-RID coverage over one leg is the choice. Additive.

rule: Two issues sharing one mechanism (node end positions read from the wrong token) are one class and one group with one generator and one shared end-of-token helper.
note: Also fixes an internal design (one helper at all 213 sites).

rule: Three editor-refactoring groups queue behind the waiting Core silent-wrong groups, applying the residue cap's reasoning to a second family.
note: Ordering only.

rule: Wrap/Extract on a selection holding a declaration referenced after the region is not offered, restoring the prior verdict now as a chore with a direction record.
note: Row cites contract §3: a regression by direction is remediated, not queued.

rule: Convert-forms writes header literals as the source token verbatim when legal in the target form, re-spells as the cooked equivalent only when not, and otherwise is not offered.
principle: A refactoring keeps the user's source spelling wherever it is legal in the target; it re-spells only when forced, else is not offered.
note: Supersedes an earlier lead plan decision (P47 D6), not an R-ruling.

rule: The seven mutation-survivor test-gap classes go on one class tracker with seven rows, drained by one tests-only group, rather than seven issues or a cell table on the pilot's tracker.
principle: Tests-only gaps found by one instrument share one tracker and one draining group, keeping the open-issue count down.
tension: R-GB: R-GB ruled survivors become test-gap issues by class, which read literally gives seven issues.; VC10: VC10 files one issue per class; here seven classes share one.

rule: Wrap in try/except is not offered when a name declared in the selected region is read after it; it is offered when nothing escapes.
