rule: The backing-field collision check gains the module host as a band chore now, turning a crash into a refusal, rather than waiting for the modifier group far down the queue.
note: User-visible effect: an ICE becomes a refusal on modules. R-JM's test is stated for false refusals; applied here to an ICE.

rule: Assigning through an import binding (a package forwarder or re-export) is a compile error with a steer to assign through the declaring module; reads stay live and a deviation row records it.
note: Write-through gives a compared surface a silent different value (T1); copy semantics changes existing programs' values (T3). The name-resolution principle 'where it cannot match Python, it refuses' also decides.

rule: The name-resolution principle is implemented as one block of five plans in fixed order: harness, then N3 alone, then N1/N2/N4/N7, then N6, then S2.
note: Supersedes R-JT's forward-read refusal in effect.

rule: The tests-only name-resolution harness group is light tier, since the full-tier reading dimensions have nothing to grade in a tests-only plan; tiers never lower once set.
principle: A tests-only plan is light whatever tier letters match, because full-tier dimensions have no subject in it.
tension: VC12: Letter (b) holds (rejected option names it) yet the group is set light via (e), which VC12 grants only upward.
note: Row cites precedent R-JR, not the departure; could be read as precedent R-JR.

rule: The class-body read residue group dissolves into the N1/N2 plan, its scope-by-host matrix becoming that plan's hand control beside the harness generator.
tension: R-JV: Supersedes R-JV's admission.; R-JW: Supersedes R-JW's new-group part.

rule: A nested type body reading the enclosing type's members by bare name is refused with a steer to qualify them, as class scopes do not nest in Python.
tension: R-JV: R-JV admitted bare class-body reads inside a lambda in an initializer.
note: Extends N1's list of bodies to nested types; Python NameError here is a scope error, not order-only, so A2 evidence counts.

rule: The type-member declaration-order group moves up to directly after the name-resolution block, and its required generator becomes an extension of the block's existing harness.
principle: A group that completes a rule's open half is scheduled right after the plans that write the rule.

rule: The name-resolution block is scheduled directly after the Core accessor group and before other pending groups, because it cures silent wrong values, common false refusals and a temporary refusal.
principle: Silent-wrong cells and the cure for a temporary refusal outrank light or crash-only groups in the queue.

rule: Two closure issues are folded into the N3 tracker and closed, a third closed as resolved by N2's refusal, and one kept open because allowlist rows cite it.
note: Also records that N2 refuses the closed issue's cell (language content).

rule: The nightly red from a None-literal receiver is pinned by a self-failing known-red draw filter keyed on that shape and citing its issue, rather than left red or spot-fixed outside its class.
note: Rejected spot fix also cites Rule 11 (CR11).

rule: Two integer-construction and primitive-method issues join the existing call-resolution group by class rather than forming a new earlier group.
principle: A cell joins the group whose contract already covers its class rather than carving seams out of that contract to land sooner.
note: CR11/CR13 are cited only against a chore, not against the rejected new group.

rule: Three public C#-only from-end index and range conversions in Core are deleted; the list's Index and Range indexers remain the C# route.
principle: A pre-1.0 public API with no consumer that cannot be made correct is deleted rather than fixed.
note: R-GW (no stability claim before 1.0) licenses the one-way door; AP 'one way to do a thing' is compatible.

rule: Six Stdlib accessor cells of the inlining class are recorded on the closed tracker only; the throw-helper shape is applied to a Stdlib accessor when a benchmark shows it hot.
principle: A performance cure is applied only where a benchmark names the code hot; an unmeasured hazard is recorded, not cured.

rule: The name-resolution harness residue gets a new tests-only group immediately after the harness group and before the N3 plan, rather than being folded into each rule plan.
The name-resolution harness cell budget rises to about 7,400 and every pruned outer kind and builtin is restored, re-ratcheting the resulting reds.
note: Rejected option is a hand re-probe, which VC11's generators-before-hand-matrices forbids.

rule: The harness-residue group is light tier although a full-tier residue criterion matches literally, overridden as for the harness group.
principle: A tests-only plan is light whatever tier letters match, because full-tier dimensions have no subject in it.
tension: VC12: VC12 makes a group full when letter (d) holds; the owner overrides it down.
note: Row acknowledges the literal match and cites R-KE as precedent.

rule: Sweep tests mute their compile output and a per-result stdout ceiling guards the class, fixing an out-of-memory in result sending; no memory sampler is added yet.
principle: Fix an instrument's class with the minimal falsifiable guard now; add measurement only when the next failure asks for it.

rule: Indexing by a slice value, negative range indexing and slicing, and slice repr are promoted to match Python in Core; slice assignment is recorded as a deviation.
principle: Promote a Python behaviour whose cure is Core-only at a low rung; record as a deviation one that needs a new compiler feature.
note: FS makes promotion an owner ruling; CV's layer ladder shapes the cure. Also creates group P81.

rule: Capturing self in a closure inside a struct method is a compile error with a named code and a steer to copy self to a local.
principle: A C# hard constraint surfaces as a named Sharpy refusal with a steer, never as a raw C# error.
note: Lowering via a copy would silently write the copy (T1).

rule: Storing to a static field or property through self or a derived type is a compile error steering to write through the declaring type, since Python's per-instance meaning cannot be matched.
note: Decided by name-resolution.md's principle ('never a different meaning; where it cannot match Python, refuse'), cited as 'the principle'; N2 is the nearest numbered rule.

rule: The constant-position validator is placed in the N1/N2/N4/N7 plan under N4, not in the modifier group whose member table it reads.
principle: A validator lives with the rule plan that defines its legality, not with the plan whose table it merely reads.

rule: A lambda whose body yields a value is refused in a slot expecting a None return, with the same type-mismatch error a wrong-typed body gets elsewhere.
principle: A lambda's body is its return value; a value-bodied lambda never silently discards its value to fit a None-returning slot.
note: Owner overruled the analysis's admit recommendation; A3 and A2 reasoning are compatible but neither forbids admission.

rule: Reading a name above its same-scope declaration while an outer binding exists is a compile error saying the name is declared later in this scope.
note: N1 (one meaning in scope) plus N5 (locals ordered); Python's UnboundLocalError agrees. Today these cells silently print the outer value.

rule: A store to a function, class, struct, enum, union, interface or alias name is refused in every store form with one code and a steer to declare a new local.
note: Confirms an existing rule row; Python would make a new local.

rule: Match and as captures are fresh per arm: without an outer binding a later read stays undefined; with one, a later read is refused as for a loop target.
note: Extends S2 to captures; Python leaks captures, even under failed guards.

rule: A builtin counts as a visible outer binding for the construct-target rule, so reusing a builtin's name as a loop target and calling it afterwards is refused.
note: Python raises TypeError at run time; Sharpy refuses at compile time (T2).

rule: A let in a for body, loop else body or match case is block-scoped, recorded as deviation rows, with a must-run harness arm.
tension: N5: N5 calls its list of designed deviations closed; block-scoped let is not on it.

rule: A nested function reading an enclosing local declared below it is refused as declared later, with or without an outer binding.
note: Cited as 'D10's rule' (R-KX). Python resolves at call time and runs.

rule: Re-declaring a name in the same scope, including a nested def over a parameter, is refused as a same-scope re-declaration rather than silently keeping the first value.
note: Today these print the first value silently (T1 also supports).

rule: A lambda-typed local reading itself stays refused, with the message steering to write a nested def instead.
principle: A Python idiom whose lowering costs complexity stays refused with a steer to the idiomatic Sharpy form until it earns the cost.
note: C# also refuses the shape (A1-compatible); AP 'not because Python has it' also supports.

rule: The block-scope deviation row widens to every binder in every block body; two same-block closure re-declaration cells go to the shadowing tracker.
tension: N5: N5's closed list of designed deviations does not name block scoping.
note: Rejected option would reverse the shadowing issue #1974 that N5 adopts.

rule: Every binding made inside a loop body is fresh per iteration, so a closure created in the loop captures that iteration's value; the deviation row widens accordingly.
note: Widens N5's first designed deviation from loop variables to all body bindings.

rule: A bare assignment over a method's name is refused with the same code as for fields and a steer to declare a new local, one verdict per member kind.
The rule against calling a local def before its definition stays def-only; a lambda-typed local read early is cited under the declared-later rule instead, with the same verdict.
principle: Each binder kind has one rule to cite.
note: Only the cited rule changes, not the verdict.

rule: A module-level initializer that reads a builtin or imported name at or before its own same-named declaration is refused as ambiguous.
note: Python reads the builtin here; N2's ambiguity test decides. The row writes this sentence into N2 itself.

rule: The emitter port to a lowering IR resumes as one full group: the IR becomes the emitter's only input, SemanticInfo freezes after validation, node-keyed tables may only fall, and new lowering facts are IR node properties.
principle: Architectural debt whose cost grows with every addition is paid down now as one group rather than drained cell by cell.
tension: CR2: CR2 still describes node-keyed SemanticInfo tables joined to MergeFrom as the sanctioned design that this ruling retires.; R-MB: R-LK says MergeFrom asserts disjointness; R-MB rewords it to equal-value tolerant.
note: Also partly superseded by R-MB (disjointness wording). Includes sequencing (process) content.

rule: Constructor-body lowering gets a new full-tier group placed directly after the IR port's row and ahead of the Core band, rather than joining a later tranche or the host-variance group.
Sharpy's V? is Optional<V>, so dict.get returns Optional; no code changes, and the anti-pattern against Optional returns is scoped to Stdlib C# APIs consumed from .NET.
principle: The spec is what the code does when they agree; a wording conflict is resolved by narrowing the wording, not by changing behaviour.
note: CV and AP today cite R-LM itself, so derivability is partly circular; the row names the CLAUDE.md anti-pattern and 'the spec wins'.

rule: Most cells of the issue become a new tests-only light group; one cell is posted to the bindings group's tracker and two become a band chore.
Each executable rule table is built as the generator row of the group that consumes it, with one tracker across them, rather than one tooling group building all tables ahead of their consumers.
principle: A generator is built by the group that consumes it, not ahead of any consumer against rules about to change.
note: Compatible with VC11 (generators first) but VC11 does not pick between the two placements.

rule: One shared codec table (name to encoding plus BOM policy) serves encode, decode and open; error handlers form a closed enumeration with a totality test; open gains errors=; chr returns a lone surrogate.
principle: A program relying on output that is a bug is not a correct program; fixing it needs no deviation record.
note: The rejected options are group placements only; the behaviour itself follows FS (values compared).

rule: Calling a nested type through self, self.N(), compiles and is lowered to the type-qualified C.N(), the same rule as other class attributes read through self.
note: N1 names self.x as a permitted spelling for class-body names in methods; python prints 3.

rule: A walrus assignment targeting a let binding is decided in the let/var plan with let's own semantics; until then the cells stay pinned Unruled and docs keep the open question.
principle: An open semantic question is pinned Unruled and decided by the feature that owns it, not by a provisional verdict that may become one-way.

rule: nonlocal x over a for, with or except target gets the same refusal and steer as global x does.
tension: A2: Python stores through for for/with targets under nonlocal, a working twin that is refused.

rule: Work runs in two lanes: the IR port's second tranche on its own PR series while the Core band runs, then the name-resolution block, one group per plan per lane.
principle: Work that touches no shared seam runs in a parallel lane rather than waiting behind unrelated work.
note: Row cites contract §11 but it does not choose serial vs parallel.

rule: The Core band groups run ahead of the codemod groups.

A walrus inside a tuple prints the plain value, not Some(value), fixed in the IR port's first tranche; the walrus site carries an explicit own-site Optional wrap so the strict-Optional guard stays unrelaxed.
principle: A failing guard is satisfied by making the emitted shape explicit, never by relaxing the guard.
tension: R-LK: Supersedes R-LK's sequencing of the first tranche after P80.
note: Mostly process (tranche ran early); classified by the user-visible tuple-print fix. Options S1/S2 are a guard choice, not law-decided.

rule: Plan bodies are capped at 20 KB excluding verification summaries, at most two verify passes run before an open finding goes to the owner, and light plans keep their adequacy pass.
principle: A process cap is set from what real instances meet, not from an aspiration none met.
note: Row cites contract §12 only for the kept summaries.

rule: Every allowlist row carries a structured issue cite, each generator has one ledger, and every cited issue must be a class issue with a cell table, replacing the per-issue row cap.
note: VC10 (file by class) decides the class-issue requirement; the ledger format is choice.

rule: Keep the dev branch and protect it to require pull requests, keep the nightly mainline soak, and enforce the 72-character commit-subject check.
One pinned CPython minor in a single file serves every workflow; the pin is the newest minor whose first bugfix release has shipped, bumped at a batching call (3.14 at the time).
principle: The Python oracle tracks the newest minor only after its first bugfix release.
tension: CR6: CR6 now says the oracle is 3.15 and never an older minor by choice; this rule deliberately chose an older minor.
note: CR6 postdates the ruling; row does not acknowledge it. R-MZ applied this rule to move to 3.15.

rule: Items already filed are closed by default; one tooling issue is placed as a band row, and three unfiled chores are left for the owner to file or drop.
MergeFrom accepts a key present in both operands when the values are equal and throws on a conflicting value, replacing the earlier disjoint wording.
principle: A merge invariant guards against conflicting facts, not against redundant agreeing ones.
tension: R-LK: R-LK said MergeFrom asserts disjointness.

rule: Permanent bug-guard rows in the stdlib CLR-throw allowlist cite one standing tracker that stays open while the file has rows and whose count may only fall.
principle: Every allowlist row cites an open issue; permanent guards cite a standing tracker rather than an uncited marker.
note: Consistent with the gap-discovery allowlist convention in CLAUDE.md Testing, which is not one of the listed law IDs.

rule: Core defines one OSError deriving from IOException, with FileNotFoundError, FileExistsError, IsADirectoryError and PermissionError deriving from it, and IOError an alias of OSError.
tension: A1: Sharpy exceptions no longer bridge to the matching .NET exception types, so .NET catch sites stop seeing them.; CR7: The spec's per-class .NET bridge was rejected and the spec rewritten rather than the implementation conforming.
note: FS compares exception hierarchy (except OSError must catch subclasses).

rule: The whole-build up-to-date check lands first, then the module-discovery cost cuts as their own group.
The walrus's role in Sharpy is reconsidered alongside the let/var and global/nonlocal binding work, not in the IR port; it is not a verdict on any cell.
principle: A construct's semantics are reconsidered with the feature family that owns them, not in an unrelated refactor.
note: Also notes let is a keyword and var is not, framed as an open design question.

rule: A nested type's bare name denotes the type wherever class-body names are visible; in methods, nested functions, lambdas or comprehension elements a bare read is refused unless an outer binding exists; spell it C.N().
note: Python raises NameError at run time where Sharpy refuses at compile time.

rule: A comprehension's walrus over a local or parameter of the same function writes through to that binding as Python does.
tension: R-MJ: Narrows R-MJ's refusal, which stays for module and enclosing outers.
note: Rejected refusal cost a working program agreeing with python; A2 twin evidence decides.

rule: Under global x, for, with and except targets naming x are refused with the steer to assign inside the loop body instead.
principle: When one member of a construct family cannot match Python, the whole family is refused with one steer rather than given split verdicts.
tension: A2: Python stores through for for/with targets under global, a working twin that is refused.

rule: A comprehension's walrus over a visible outer name that is read after it is refused by the S2 rule.
tension: R-MH: R-MH admits the same-function case this rule refused.
note: Row's door text: A can be lifted later; B/D change printed values.

rule: The live charter is extended in place for the new call rather than starting a new round charter.
A statement ahead of self.__init__(...) or super().__init__() in a constructor is refused with one diagnostic steering the user to move the call first.
principle: A C# hard constraint surfaces as a named Sharpy refusal with a steer, not as an emulating lowering.
note: C# constructor initializers must precede the body; Python allows statements first.

rule: Constructor-initializer totality becomes a new full-tier compiler-lane group after the IR port's third tranche, ahead of name resolution.
note: Row cites 'the P85 precedent' (R-LL) without the ruling ID.

rule: The real-literal fit check unwraps a unary sign as the integer check does, so a signed float literal that was refused now compiles.
True division and a zero base raised to a negative power raise ZeroDivisionError with Python's messages, routed through Builtins helpers as floor division is.
note: Rejected option was placement only; spec states raise.

rule: A new light group makes the parser accept what the spec states, with a parse-verdict roster, absorbing a related issue as a cell.
note: Behavioural content (parser follows spec) is CR7; the ruled choice is placement.

rule: A per-alternative guard in an or-pattern must be parenthesised as (p if g); the contradicting example is rewritten and the parser is unchanged.
note: Door inferred from 'additive later'.

rule: Named-field tuple patterns like case (x=0.0, y=0.0): are implemented, binding by field name and lowered to positional ValueTuple matching.
note: Owner called the rejected 'mark planned' option legitimate, so CR7 may not strictly decide.

rule: functools.partial is not provided; docs mark it superseded by _ partial application.
Dataclasses get a synthesized copy(**changes) member with one keyword-only optional parameter per field.
principle: A documented feature is implemented rather than having the documents that describe it rewritten away.
note: Python's twin is dataclasses.replace, a different spelling.

rule: Keywordless inferred class fields stay unsupported; the spec sentence gets a pending marker and is rewritten to let/var/const spellings by the bindings plan.
note: B1/B6 are earlier design decisions, not R-numbered rulings.

rule: Overload resolution prefers the candidate with no defaulted parameters, as the spec states, instead of reporting ambiguity.
Constructor piping is allowed: x |> C(args) means C(x, args), and the spec limitation is removed.
principle: Any callee kind a call accepts is accepted by the pipe operator; no callee is special-cased.
tension: CR7: The spec's stated limitation is removed instead of the implementation conforming to it.

rule: The IR port's done-when covers type, symbol, layout or diagnostic facts; module layouts stay layout facts; the third tranche splits the type half of operator and type-test lowerings.
The cell budget and refusal-rate ceilings are derived from the fixture corpus so no single fixture moves them, with a planted spike as the mutation test.
principle: Instrument thresholds are derived from the corpus, never re-pinned per fixture.
note: Mutation requirement follows VC2.

rule: The CPython oracle moves from 3.14 to 3.15 now that 3.15.1 has shipped, and each resulting stdout difference becomes a cell, never a snapshot update.
note: Precedent R-LZ cited; CR6 now states it.

rule: A band chore deletes a dead source file and moves old stdlib batch plans under the process plans directory; an unnamed isalnum cell is dropped.
note: Resolves chores left open by R-MA.

rule: Three silent-wrong walrus-in-dict-spread-comprehension rows stay allowlisted until the S2 refusal lands, rather than landing that refusal before the mainline merge.
principle: A known silent-wrong cell may wait on its class fix when a sibling already carries the same missing refusal.
tension: T1: Ships known silently wrong values to mainline pending the fix.

rule: requests' files= keeps path strings and returns Err(RequestException), recorded as a deviation row.
note: FS: unlisted surface is DEVIATION; choice among a/b/c is partly design.

rule: open and the archive openers accept every mode Python accepts, delivered as a new two-phase group.
principle: A Python-surface API accepts the full Python argument domain rather than a subset with a recorded deviation.
tension: AP: Leans toward adding surface because Python has it.

rule: The ConnectionError exception family waits for the namespace-layout group; TimeoutError and EnvironmentError go to the builtin-exceptions group, subject to its own decision on which names Core declares.
note: Placement only; depends on R-NN.

rule: sys.exit raises SystemExit; the generated entry point catches it and returns its code as the process exit code; a bare except Exception still catching it remains a recorded deviation.
principle: Move toward Python's run-time behaviour where it needs no spec rewrite; a remaining gap that would need one stays a recorded deviation.
tension: SPEC:exceptions: The spec's 'No BaseException' section is why except Exception still catches SystemExit, kept as a deviation.
note: Main effect matches Python (print runs, code returned); except Exception catching SystemExit deviates. Option (b) rejected partly to avoid rewriting the spec.

rule: open, Path, xml and requests all resolve encoding names through one shared codec resolver; .NET-only aliases are lost at the xml and requests seams, and two cells are deviation rows.
note: AP 'one way to do the same thing' picks one resolver over per-seam switches. Row says one-way for the lost aliases; deviation cells cite R-CI and Axiom 1.

rule: Decimal zero divided by zero raises ZeroDivisionError, recorded as a deviation row, instead of adding decimal.InvalidOperation for the undefined case.
principle: A missing Python exception subclass is a recorded deviation rather than a new type when the raised base type still catches it.
tension: FS: FS marks exception TYPE as COMPARED with divergences going to an issue, but this records a deviation row instead.
note: Not acknowledged as a departure from FS. CPython raises DivisionUndefined (subclass of both InvalidOperation and ZeroDivisionError), so except ZeroDivisionError behaves the same.

rule: Compiler tools multi-target net10.0 and net11.0, compiled programs keep defaulting to net10.0, emission is unchanged, and a light group first measures the work and gain of a net11/C# 15 migration.
principle: Move the runtime target of compiled programs only after a measured smoke of its cost and gain; tooling may multi-target ahead.
note: Door two-way stated for A1 only. Option given as A(1), B, C.

rule: One band chore audits every Stdlib module that has a CPython namesake and completes the third-party notices file; the pre-tag deadline is dropped because the release already exists.
note: Licensing/notice completeness; SPDX id decided by R-NO.

rule: The procedure-bytes scorecard key also counts the verification contract and the process README, with the baseline raised once by their size.
A new issue is filed as the Format Selection refused-work tracker, sweep allowlist rows re-cite it, and the old issue closes once its ceilings-from-corpus ask is confirmed landed.
note: Could be read as VC10 (file by class), but VC10 does not pick filing a new tracker over retitling the old one.

rule: The exception-group handler group is promoted to the full tier under criterion (c) because its remaining seam is in lowering; tiers move only upward.
note: VC12 (c) makes a Lowering seam full; '(c)' in the row is VC12's criterion letter but VC12 is not named, so law_cited false.

rule: Core declares a Python builtin exception name only where a Core or Stdlib site raises it or an existing type derives from it; one deviation row records all other names as ruled absences.
principle: A Python builtin name enters Core only when a Core/Stdlib site uses it; the rest are recorded absences.
note: AP 'no add X because Python has it' rules out (a); (c) none would drop names in use. Each added name reserves the spelling (SPY0212).

rule: Packages carrying CPython-derived code (Core, Stdlib, Cli) declare the SPDX licence Python-2.0, the full CPython licence stack the notices reproduce, not PSF-2.0.
principle: Licence metadata names the exact upstream licence stack whose text the shipped notices reproduce.
note: Two-way until each release.

rule: The operator-lowering table stays a table in tranche 3, read by the lowering pass and const eligibility; deriving the kinds in the pass and deleting the table waits for tranche 4.
principle: Transport an existing structure intact first; redesign it in a later tranche.
note: Also a scheduling decision.

rule: The array-bridge conversion and sequence-materialization table leave tranche 3 for tranche 4 because they need their own generator over position, route and conversion.
note: VC11: a 3-axis matrix needs a generator first; deferring is the consequence.

rule: socket.error.errno is the platform's native error code, compared with Python where .NET's SocketError round trip is exact; all other cases are one recorded deviation row; the fidelity table gains the row.
principle: Promote a surface to COMPARED where .NET reproduces Python's value exactly; record the rest as one deviation row.
note: Promotion of an unlisted surface under FS's procedure (R-CM); FS permits but does not decide promotion.

rule: Socket bad-type/protocol errors keep .NET codes as a deviation since mapping would corrupt genuine ones; errno is int or None, None on timeout; an unknown host raises gaierror with -2.
principle: Never remap an error code when the mapping would rewrite genuine occurrences of the target code.
note: E2/E3 match Python (FS: exception type compared); E1 deviates, decided by T1 (no silently wrong value).

rule: The membership group runs ahead of the charter queue in its own lane with tier full, criteria (b) and (c).
note: Queue jump is a choice; the tier itself follows VC12 (b),(c).

rule: bool and decimal needles tested for membership in range or bytes stay refused at compile time, because no implicit conversion to int exists; the deviation row is reworded.
tension: R-NW: bytes accepts an int needle while a bool needle (an int in Python) is refused.
note: Row names 'the implicit-conversion rule' but not the spec file.

rule: A T | None membership needle is accepted and answers False when None; a literal None needle is accepted only where the element type is optional and refused elsewhere, including str and bytes.
principle: A literal None compared against something that statically cannot hold None is a compile error; a possibly-None value is accepted.
tension: R-NX: Here a None needle answers False, while for IPv4Network/IPv6Network/EmailMessage a None needle raises AttributeError.; R-OS: R-OS later makes a None needle into a plain value-type Contains parameter raise TypeError rather than answer False.
note: Supersedes earlier same-day unnumbered answers. Python gives False for None in a list and TypeError for str; refusing a literal follows A3/T2 in spirit.

rule: A bytes container accepts a bytes needle (subsequence test) and an int needle (single byte) for membership; the spec row is amended.
tension: CR7: The spec row is amended to fit the ruling rather than the implementation to the spec.; R-NU: int needle admitted while bool needle refused.
note: Python's twin decides; no A1 conflict.

rule: A None needle tested for membership in IPv4Network, IPv6Network or EmailMessage raises AttributeError as CPython does; separately, the scorecard allowlist-rows baseline is set to 546.
tension: R-NV: Built-in containers answer False for a None needle; these Stdlib types raise.
note: Second half (baseline 546) is a test-instrument decision. FS compares exception types for Stdlib.

rule: Enums are treated as value types throughout the compiler, not only at membership checks, which moves the emitted nullable shape of Enum | None; a third plan-verification pass is allowed.
note: Row says 'one-way in effect'. CR11 (fix the class) picks compiler-wide over membership-only; A1 says enums are CLR value types. Placement superseded by R-OQ; work confirmed by R-OU.

rule: A user class defining __iter__ but not __contains__ answers in / not in by iterating; a class with neither stays refused.
tension: R-OA: The analogous Python fallback via __len__ + __getitem__ is refused.
note: Rejected keeping the refusal with a deviation row.

rule: A class with only __len__ and __getitem__ stays refused for in / not in, with a deviation row explaining the index need not be an integer nor dense.
principle: A Python fallback protocol is admitted only when the declared dunders statically guarantee its contract; legacy implicit protocols stay refused.
tension: R-NZ: The __iter__ fallback is admitted as CPython does, this one is not.; A2: Python has a twin here and would run the program.

rule: A T | None is falsy when None or when its payload is falsy, in every truth-testing position and in bool(x), as in Python; T? stays truthy exactly when it is Some.
tension: CR7: Rejects the spec's existing null-check rule; the spec is rewritten to the ruling.
note: Python twin decides for T | None; T? has no twin.

rule: Container-side operations with a T | None operand stay allowed and a None raises Python's TypeError; ordering on a T | None, first refused, is now allowed with a warning per the later nullability principle.
principle: A possibly-None operand into an operation Python accepts stays legal and fails like Python at run time.
tension: R-OP: R-OP replaced the compile-time refusal of ordering with a warning plus run-time TypeError.; T2: Keeping run-time TypeError over a compile-time refusal pulls against T2.

rule: hash(x) accepts a None value instead of raising TypeError.
note: Python hashes None; consistent with R-OP's 'dict keys always allowed'.

rule: The three membership-related issues form one group directly after the membership group, built on its generator, rather than being scattered across three groups.
The issue goes first in its group and that group moves to the head of the Core lane, rather than a band fix for five routes.
The compiler lane order is fixed as a specific sequence of six groups, with tranche 4 of the operator group before the next group.
A float32 variable accepts **= with a float literal, as its other augmented operators do; a decimal variable with **= 2.0 is refused at compile time.
principle: Members of one operator family treat a literal operand the same way on a given type.
note: float32 has no Python twin; Decimal ** float is a TypeError in Python, so the decimal refusal moves it to compile time.

rule: The socket cells get their own tracker and light group; remaining errno cells and constant values stay deviation rows; import errno and exception args/strerror go to other named groups.
note: VC10 (file by class) supports a separate tracker but does not clearly decide.

rule: The scorecard issue splits by class: the Markdown-reading checks become their own tracker and group with one CommonMark reader; three cells go to the band; the rest stay.
A conditional expression against a generic-parameter slot is one class; the existing issue is retitled and stays in its group instead of opening a second tracker.
Conditional-expression and fresh-walrus needles are outside the membership plan's contract and are tracked under the nullability group; a fourth plan-verification pass is allowed.
tension: VC12: Repeated extra verify-plan passes sit uneasily with VC12's convergence rule.
note: VC11 one group per plan favours not widening the plan.

rule: is / is not with an operand statically typed as an enum compares by member, like CPython singletons; members of two different enum types are never identical; other cases are a deviation row.
principle: Enum members are identities: is on enums compares by member even though the CLR representation is a boxed value type.
tension: R-OX: R-OX makes is identity only and value-type operands always False; enums are its one ruled exception.; A1: Under A1 boxed value types are never reference-equal.
note: Could be argued as RR (zero-cost compile-time rewrite reconciling A1 and A2), but RR's listed mechanisms don't clearly cover it. Landed as a no-plan lane.

rule: == between members of two different int-backed enum types answers False and != answers True, both operands evaluated once, rather than a compile-time refusal.
tension: R-OW: R-OW treats int-backed enums as IntEnum for ordering, under which cross-type == would compare by value.; R-QG: Amended for string-backed enums to compare by value.
note: Matches plain Enum, not IntEnum.

rule: Value-ness agrees with the emitted C# type for constructed generic structs, struct-constrained type parameters and Self in a struct, at every reader, as already ruled for enums; a fifth verification pass is allowed.
note: Placement moved by R-OQ; confirmed by R-OU.

rule: T never holds None; T | None is loose (behaves as T, warns where None fails, fails as CPython, never NRE); T? is strict (Some/None() only, refused until narrowed, x == None steered to is None).
principle: Python's union spelling is loose and fails as CPython at run time with warnings; Sharpy's own Optional spelling is strict and refused until narrowed.
tension: T2: Loose T | None prefers warnings plus run-time TypeError over compile-time errors.; A3: A3 says None requires opt-in via T?, while T | None is a second, looser opt-in.; AP: Two nullable spellings with different strictness risks 'multiple ways to do the same thing'.; R-OC: Supersedes R-OC's compile-time refusal of ordering.
note: Foundational; T3 (correct programs keep running) supports the loose half. Rewrites nullable_types.md and logical_operators.md.

rule: The membership plan keeps only membership work; the value-ness work moves to the nullability tracker under its principle, and generator cells needing it stay known-red citing that tracker.
tension: R-NY: Supersedes R-NY's placement.; R-OO: Supersedes R-OO's placement.

rule: A sixth plan-verification pass is allowed after the plan split discarded the fifth pass's converged verdict.
tension: VC12: VC12 says the verify loop ends on a decision, yet passes kept being granted.

rule: A None needle passed to an opaque __contains__ or CLR Contains whose parameter is a plain value type raises TypeError at that boundary, as for any T | None flowing into a plain T, landed with the general boundary work.
tension: R-NV: R-NV answered False for a T | None needle; this raises for opaque value-type receivers.
note: Row quotes the nullability principle verbatim without naming R-OP.

rule: The nullability work is one group, re-chartered as 'every cell of the nullability ledger matches its target', in four tranches each with its own plan and gate.
Value-ness matches the emitted C# type compiler-wide, and the checker stays loose on such operands: programs that run today keep running, gain a warning and raise TypeError on None.
tension: T2: Rejects the compile-time refusals the plan proposed in favour of run-time TypeError.
note: T3 also supports keeping today's running programs.

rule: Two new default-on warning codes: one for an operation on T | None that fails on None, one for a T | None flowing into a plain T where the compiler inserts a check.
principle: Each distinct failure mechanism gets its own suppressible code; existing codes are not reused for a new meaning.
note: Codes from the 0710-0799 range.

rule: Ordering within one int-backed enum type keeps .NET order, as IntEnum, recorded as a deviation; ordering across two enum types is refused at compile time.
tension: R-ON: Cross-type == on int-backed enums follows plain Enum (False), while ordering follows IntEnum.
note: Row notes (a) records the status quo (T3); cross-type refusal turns Python's TypeError into a compile error (T2).

rule: x is not <type> is refused with the existing type-test code steering to not isinstance; is / is not are identity only, never a type test or __eq__; value-type operands are always False with a warning.
principle: An operator keeps one meaning; a likely misuse is refused with a steer, reusing the existing code for the same mistake.
tension: R-OM: Enums compare by member under is, the one acknowledged exception.
note: Enum exception confirmed by owner.

rule: Each link of a comparison chain has exactly its binary twin's outcome: value, refusal code or internal error; a chain over a class without __eq__ is refused wherever the binary comparison is.
principle: A desugared form inherits its primitive's outcome exactly (value, refusal code, internal error); no form-specific refusal or exemption.
tension: T3: Chains that ran and printed a value are now refused.; R-PI: Depends on the refusal of == without __eq__, which Python answers by identity.
note: Close in spirit to N7 (spelling never changes the verdict) and T4, but neither speaks of operator desugarings.

rule: A stage-0 allowlist row is one fact and one cause; a bulk row is valid only while its cells share both; extending a generator extends its allowlist file; a compiler-crashing form is a known-red row, not an exclusion.
principle: Every known failure is a counted, cited row with one fact and one cause; nothing failing is excluded from a generator.
note: Refines VC11's allowlist mechanics; VC11 does not fix row granularity, so the owner picked.

rule: The membership generator draws its axes from compiler enumerations by reflection, crosses blocks pairwise with operand forms and hoist kinds, and rules out the full cube and chains longer than three links by cost.
principle: Generator axes are images of compiler enumerations; combinatorial cost is cut by pairwise crossing, never by hand-picked cells.
note: The reflection-sourced axes are VC11-derivable; the pairwise cut and length bound are the owner's choice.

rule: The stage-0 allowlist baseline was raised step by step to the count one-row-per-fact-and-cause gives at each tip, without registering the allowlist as a seed harness.
note: VC11 prescribes raising allowlist_rows_outside_seed with the owner's word; seed registration is owner-ruled and was declined.

rule: The membership generator's CI cost is accepted; extra compiler shards and a 40-minute PR shard limit are added in separate changes rather than cutting the generated facts.
principle: Coverage the contract requires is kept; CI capacity is raised to carry it, never coverage cut to fit CI.

rule: A chain middle operand that is also an in-needle is typed as its left link's binary comparison types it and cast to the in-slot only where the in-link reads it.
note: Fixes a wrong False versus CPython True; also moves 28 cells' refusal code to the twin's code.

rule: A constant middle needle in a chain is admitted by its value where it fits the in-slot, as the standalone membership test is, and always cast at the in-read; out-of-range constants are refused.
note: Follows the chain-link-equals-binary-twin rule; the row cites the standalone form, not R-OY.

rule: In a comparison chain each link reads a shared operand as its binary twin would: is-None links read it un-narrowed, others narrowed; it is evaluated once, typed by its first reader, converted at later reads.
note: Option letter is A of A/B/C; rejected a deviation row and a refusal.

rule: The one-decider, class-own-__iter__ clause is split out of its group into a new group with a fixed issue order.
The membership/nullability lane was ordered as three groups in sequence.
tension: R-PM: R-PM supersedes the lane's position, keeping only relative order.

rule: == and != on a type declaring no __eq__ stay refused, with one rule and one code for every spelling, wrapper and site, plus a deviations row and spec line.
principle: Absent a declared equality, comparison is refused rather than defaulting to identity; the refusal is uniform across spellings and kept relaxable.
tension: R-PL: R-PL adopts identity-before-__eq__ semantics for containers, while plain == never falls back to identity.; RR: Reference identity is a zero-cost .NET default that could reconcile A1 and A2, yet the refusal was chosen.
note: T2/T4 are compatible but do not decide refusal versus identity; row flags a caveat that may bring option c back.

rule: A sequence-repetition count is an int slot: widths implicitly widening to int are accepted; other widths are refused with an int(n) steer.
principle: Builtin operand slots are statically typed: implicit widening is accepted, narrowing needs an explicit conversion, never a checked run-time conversion.
note: T2 rules out the checked-conversion option; (a) versus refusing all non-int is the owner's pick.

rule: Ordering comparisons on a string-backed enum are refused in Semantic, as CPython's plain Enum does; int-backed enums keep value ordering.
principle: Where Python's twin is ambiguous, choose the refusal that can later be relaxed over a one-way runtime ordering.
tension: R-QG: R-QG treats string-backed enums as StrEnum for ==, while this ruling treats them as plain Enum for ordering.; R-OW: Int-backed enums order by value, string-backed do not.

rule: Container search and container equality check identity before __eq__ for reference-type elements, as CPython documents; value types keep Equals; NaN-by-identity is a deviations row.
principle: Where CPython documents a semantics observable through user __eq__, Sharpy matches it for reference types; value types keep .NET Equals.
tension: R-PI: Identity semantics are adopted in containers while == without __eq__ is refused rather than identity-based.
note: A promotion to COMPARED under FS; FS requires a ruling for promotion but does not decide it.

rule: The next arc is: values ready before use, order-free name resolution, global/nonlocal, then let/var/const bindings; the membership/nullability lane follows later in its prior relative order.
principle: User-facing language features outrank deeper correctness digs in scheduling, subject to dependency order.
tension: R-PH: Supersedes R-PH's placement of the membership lane next.
note: Dependency (N3 before N1 forward reads) fixed P77 ahead of P78.

rule: The initialization group's stage 0 is a new generated test type with its own allowlist, and the outside-seed allowlist baseline rises by the measured red count.
note: VC11 describes exactly this; seed registration and other pool options not approved.

rule: Harness rows failing because a later module variable is invisible are re-cited to the order-free name-resolution issue; the initialization group does not take N1 for module variables.
note: N1's text names the issue that implements it.

rule: An initializer that throws during the load sweep ends the program before main with the original exception, never TypeInitializationException; retry remains observable only on lazy hosts.
note: N3 runs initializers at load before main and retries on next read; the original-exception choice follows CV's Python exceptions.

rule: The no-initializer cell is moved out of the initialization group to another issue unruled, and the group's issue closes on its own criteria.
note: The cell was later ruled by R-QI.

rule: A plan may depart from the charter's prescribed emission where a refuted cell requires it, provided ruled behaviour stays fixed and each departure is named in the plan.
principle: Rulings bind observable behaviour, not emission shape; a plan may reshape implementation if each departure is named.

rule: Whether an initialization cycle is visible at compile time is decided by a total map classifying each expression child position as conditional or unconditional, so non-const visible cycles are compile errors too.
note: Rejected option made non-const visible cycles run-time NameErrors, against N3 and T2; the roster/totality mechanism echoes VC11.

rule: A property passed as a ref, out or in operand is refused at the checker in every host, whether or not it has a default.
note: C# refuses properties as by-reference arguments; door read from 'Relaxable'.

rule: The initialization group's benchmark acceptance records every ratio in the pull request and blocks nothing; the owner judges cost at review.
principle: Performance cost is reported and judged by the owner, not enforced by an automatic threshold.

rule: An out operand naming a module or static value is a temporary stored on return before the value's initializer runs, and the storage itself once ready; the arm follows the value's state, not its host.
principle: Readiness-dependent behaviour is keyed on the value's state, never its host; residual differences are accepted and named in the spec.
tension: T3: Four programs change their output as accepted residue.

rule: A store to a module or static value before its initializer is kept and visible, and the initializer still runs at its declared position and replaces it; an initializer is never skipped.
tension: R-PY: Across classes, the class-as-a-unit sweep governs instead of declaration order.; T4: Module values and class values follow different sweep rules.
note: T1 forbids a skipped initializer; N3's top-to-bottom load picks declaration order over initialize-before-first-use.

rule: A closed generic type runs all its initializers in declaration order on its first use, wherever that use is; a cross-type read-back NameError is accepted residue.
note: A1 names generic instantiation and type initialization as inherited CLR behaviour.

rule: Every class sweeps all its static values in declaration order when first touched or when the module sweep reaches it, whichever comes first; module values keep declaration-order sweep with on-demand forward reads.
tension: R-PW: Declaration order with replacement governs module values but not cross-class order.; R-QA: R-QA departs from C# touch-order results this ruling otherwise inherits.
note: Owner chose 'C# order'; A1 now states this default.

rule: N3's emission does what C# does unless N3 forbids it: a self-store inside an initializer is visible then replaced; a self-read before any store is a cycle, NameError or SPY0278, never a default.
principle: Inherit C# run-time behaviour unless N3 forbids it; silent default values are never acceptable.
note: This ruling is the source of A1's run-time-default text; judged against the law as written today.

rule: Two classes whose initializers read each other's values raise NameError whichever is touched first, including touch orders that print correct values today.
tension: T3: Programs that print correct values today now raise; the row names this departure.; R-PY: Departs from the C# class-initialization order R-PY inherits.
note: T1 forbids a value depending on which initializer ran first; A1 lets N3 override C#. Departure from C# acknowledged.

rule: A ring of non-const values is a compile error unless a same-module store names one of its values; a ring kept alive only by another module's store is refused, a recorded false refusal.
principle: A rare false refusal is accepted to keep cycles compile-time errors.
tension: T3: A correct program kept alive by a cross-module store is falsely refused.

rule: One plan received three extra verify-plan passes beyond the standing two, each after a narrow revision; the standing two-pass rule holds for every other plan.
principle: A one-off extension of a process limit is spent, never precedent.
tension: R-LW: Exceeds R-LW's two-pass limit for this plan.
note: VC12's convergence says the loop ends on a decision; row acknowledges the departure as spent. Exception is against R-LW precedent as much as VC12.

rule: The outside-seed allowlist baseline was set to the measured red count at each stage-0 commit of the initialization group, without seed registration.
A class-body initializer's bare read of a later non-compile-time const of its own type, while an outer binding holds the name, stays a compile error until N2's own code replaces it.
note: Supersedes a lead ruling that let such cells run behind allowlisted rows.

rule: The membership needle side table moves onto an IR node and its pin returns; the side-table field-count pin is raised only on the owner's quoted word.
principle: A ratchet pin rises only on the owner's quoted word; an exception granted once is not precedent.
note: Also consistent with CR2's materialization guard.

rule: == between two different string-backed enum types compares by value as StrEnum does; is and is not never run a user __eq__.
principle: Enum equality follows the Python enum flavour whose backing matches; identity operators never dispatch to user code.
tension: R-PK: R-PK refuses ordering on string-backed enums as plain Enum, while this treats them as StrEnum for equality.; R-ON: Amends R-ON, which stands only for int-backed enums.

rule: The name-resolution sweep's hang timeout and job limit were raised for the initialization group, then the sweep is to be sharded and both limits restored.
principle: Raise CI limits to admit necessary coverage, then shard to win them back.
note: Same pattern as R-PC.

rule: A module-level or static declaration with no initializer is refused in Semantic with a steer to an explicit zero or None initializer.
note: A3 requires initialization at declaration; T2 beats the NameError option; door read from 'relaxable to (b)'.

rule: An in modifier at a call site on a literal or other non-name expression is refused; on any const it runs, with the keyword dropped for a compile-time constant.
note: N4 rules out treating literal and computed consts differently; admitting literals is rejected by analogy with ref. Outcome mixes admit and refuse.

rule: A member store into a struct-typed property value is refused in Semantic; a method call on it keeps C#'s copy semantics, documented in the struct spec.
note: C# refuses the same store (CS1612); copy-in/copy-out rejected as a one-way runtime change.

rule: An assignment evaluates its value before its target's subexpressions, as CPython does, hoisting the value only where the target has effects.
principle: Evaluation order observable through side effects follows Python where a cheap hoist reconciles it, rather than inheriting C#'s order.
tension: A1: C# evaluates target subexpressions first; the row does not name this as an A1 departure.; FS: Evaluation order is an unlisted surface, DEVIATION by default; this acts as a promotion.
note: RR's zero-cost bridge may cover it, making it derivable; the row does not argue either way.

rule: An observer property's storage is opaque: its underscore-prefixed backing name is refused in every position; the mixed form keeps its documented backing name.
principle: Compiler-synthesized storage is not nameable from user code unless documented; start with the relaxable refusal.
note: Door read from 'relaxable to (b)'.

rule: Two cells leave their planned groups now as no-plan lanes, each with a generated test and a mutation record; cells touching Semantic stay put while another group is in flight.
principle: Contained fixes ship early as no-plan lanes unless they touch a seam an in-flight group owns.

rule: A new full-tier group is created for observer-property storage, tracker filed, scheduled in the compiler lane after the IR tranche.
note: Tier letters (c, d) are VC12's criteria; the row cites them by letter, not section.

rule: One group is light-tier although the criteria read full, scheduled after the rule table; another is light before the IR tranche; tiers only move upward once planning begins.
principle: The owner may set a tier below the criteria at charter time; after planning begins tiers only rise.
tension: VC12: VC12 makes a group full when any criterion holds; the row acknowledges the criteria read full (b).; CR13: CR13 says the tier is a charter fact never lowered.
note: Departure acknowledged in the row.

rule: The allowlist-issue-state CI job keeps running on mainline unchanged; its red was resolved by retargeting Dependabot to dev.
Inside an async def, only out operands, member stores and mutating calls are hoisted; a ref operand evaluates in operand order as in a plain def.
tension: CR7: The spec is edited by ruling; the row acknowledges rule 7.
note: Row cites R-PZ's principle, which A1 now codifies; precedent R-PZ would also fit.
